challenges.name: evolving-event-schemas
challenges.title: Evolving event schemas without breaking consumers
challenges.description: Two statements on the ProgressRecorded change at CodeDev: a consumer whose validator rejected an additive field, and a producer change that a schema compatibility check accepted.

questions.explanation: True. .strict() makes zod reject any key the schema does not declare, so a purely additive producer change sends every event to the DLQ. Without it, z.object strips unknown keys by default and still enforces the declared ones: courseId stays required, so an event without it still fails validation. That is a tolerant reader: strict about the fields this consumer uses, indifferent to fields it does not know. The misconception is that tolerance means accepting anything; a tolerant reader still rejects events that lack what it needs.

questions.question:
Proposed change to ProgressRecorded (same version number, same field names):

-  percent: number;   // 0..100
+  percent: number;   // 0..1, a fraction for the mobile progress ring

CI output:
schema-check ProgressRecorded: proposed schema is COMPATIBLE with all registered versions (mode: FULL_TRANSITIVE)

Certificate consumer:
if (event.percent >= 100) await issueCertificate(event.enrollmentId);

Statement: "Because the schema check accepted the change as compatible with every registered version, the certificate consumer keeps issuing certificates after the producer deploys it."
questions.explanation: False. A compatibility check compares structure: field names, types, required or optional. percent is a number before and after, so every mode passes. What changed is the meaning, and no schema check sees meaning: after the deploy a finished course has percent 1, the condition percent >= 100 is never true, and certificates stop with no error at all. The fix is a new field name (for example progressRatio) or a new version, never a new meaning for an old name. The misconception is that a green registry check proves consumers are safe; it proves only that they can still parse the bytes.
